arguments.summary: A coordinated attack originating from a compromised finance workstation (WS-FIN-042) led to credential theft, lateral movement, and exposure of privileged account admin_jsmith. The attacker used Cobalt Strike C2 infrastructure, performed internal reconnaissance, and successfully exfiltrated credentials that appeared on a dark web paste. Multiple anomalous access attempts followed, including from an IT workstation (WS-IT-101), indicating active lateral movement. Immediate credential revocation was executed based on high-fidelity indicators.

timeline.description: Initial compromise: WS-FIN-042 establishes outbound HTTPS connection to suspicious IP 198.51.100.23 (Cobalt Strike C2).
IDS alerts on Cobalt Strike beaconing from WS-FIN-042 to 198.51.100.23.
Failed Kerberos TGT request from WS-FIN-042, indicating credential dumping attempt.
Lateral movement via SMB from WS-FIN-042 to file server 10.0.5.50.
SSH brute-force detected from 10.0.5.14 (WS-FIN-042) targeting bastion host. Incident INC-2026-1203A created.
Dark web monitoring detects admin_jsmith credentials in breach dump. Hash matches AD. Incident INC-2026-1203B created.
Anomalous Kerberos TGS request for admin_jsmith from unassigned device WS-IT-101 (10.0.6.99). Incident INC-2026-1203C created.
UEBA system flags admin_jsmith with anomaly score 0.92 due to off-hours access, unusual geolocation, and lateral movement.
Credential revocation for admin_jsmith completed. 3 sessions and 2 API keys terminated.
Full EPP scan of WS-FIN-042 detects Linux dropper /var/spool/cron/.job.

rule Linux_Cron_Persistence_Dropper {
    meta:
        description = "Detects suspicious binary in cron-like path commonly used by Linux malware"
        author = "SOC_Team"
        reference = "S0392"
        date = "2026-04-11"
    strings:
        $s1 = "/var/spool/cron" nocase
        $s2 = "nohup" nocase
        $s3 = "wget" nocase
        $s4 = "chmod +x" nocase
    condition:
        all of ($s*) and filename matches /\.job|\.tmp|\.dat$/
}

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_HTTPS_Profile {
    meta:
        description = "Detects memory patterns of Cobalt Strike beacon using HTTPS C2 with specific URI and header structure"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "ET TROJAN Cobalt Strike Beacon C2 Activity"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $x86_jmp = { E9 ?? ?? ?? ?? }
        $config_start = "#M"
        $uri_path = "/index.php"
        $header_accept = "Accept: */*\r\n"
    condition:
        uint16(0) == 0x5a4d and
        $x86_jmp and
        $config_start and
        $uri_path and
        $header_accept
}

arguments.rule_content:
title: Multiple Tor Exit Node Scans to Single Internal Host
id: 5a7d1a2b-8f3e-4c1d-9c2a-1f4e5a6b7c8d
status: experimental
description: Detects distributed scanning activity from multiple Tor exit nodes to a single internal host within a short timeframe.
references:
    - https://www.torproject.org/docs/exit-addresses
author: SOC Team
logsource:
    category: firewall
    product: generic
detection:
    tor_exit:
        src_ip|contains: '185.220.101.'
    scan_activity:
        dst_ip: '*'
        event_type: port_scan
    timeframe: 5m
    condition: tor_exit and scan_activity by dst_ip | count(src_ip) by dst_ip > 5
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate security scanning from known Tor-using researchers
level: high
